items.actClause:
AN ACT relating to requiring home health aides and nurse's aides to receive
training in working with lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender individuals
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2534

SPONSOR: RIVERA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act relating to requiring home health aides and nurse's aides to
receive training in working with lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender
individuals

 
PURPOSE:

To require the Department of Health to add a "working with LGBTQ+ indi-
viduals" module to the Home Care Curriculum and the Nurse Aide Training
Program to help ensure that LGBTQ+ individuals of all ages get better,
more culturally competent care.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 requires that the Commissioner of Health, in consultation with
the Commissioner of Education, shall develop a training program that
focuses on working with LGBTQ+ individuals as part of the state approved
education or training programs required for certification of home health
aides, personal care aides, personal care staff, and certified nurse's
aides.

Section 2 sets the requirements of the training program which include
but are not limited to (1) an explanation of the terms lesbian, gay,
bisexual, and transgender, (2) a understanding of why LGBTQ+ individuals
may hide their identity, (3) incorporate LGBTQ+ concerns into person-di-
rected care, so that each individual can make the best decisions for
their own situation, (4) specific information designed for staff working
in nursing care or other residential care settings, (5) unique needs of
LGBTQ+ individuals and older adults, (6) an overview of the various
rights and protections extended to LGBTQ+ individuals, (7) best prac-
tices for creating communities welcoming to LGBTQ+ individuals including
older adults, their loved ones, and their caregivers, (8) practical tips
from experts about how to ask questions related to sexual orientation
and gender identity and understand why these questions are important for
all service organizations, (9) the nuances of asking questions related
to sexual orientation and gender identity to LGBTQ+ individuals, (10)
how to respectfully respond to questions and concerns that arise in
these conversations, (11) best practices for providing transgender
affirming care.

Sections 3 requires that the training unit be developed within six
months of the effective date of this bill and shall be required for all
certifications and recertifications of home health aides, personal care
aides, personal care staff, and certified nurse's aides.

Section 4 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

A visit to a healthcare facility can make someone uncomfortable for a
variety of reasons. This is especially the case for many LGBTQ+ individ-
uals who may have difficulty finding health care where they feel
included and accepted. A 2017 CAP survey provided evidence that LGBTQ+
individuals experience discrimination in healthcare settings.  Some
individuals have reported being refused care because of their sexual
orientation or gender identity. These issues extend beyond the patients
themselves. Family members, partners and other loved ones have reported
being refused recognition by healthcare providers.

In many other cases, staff who did not intend any harm can cause prob-
lems from simple mistakes that occur due to lack of understanding or
experience interacting with LGBTQ+ individuals. Many LGBTQ+ individuals
have unique life experiences that require different practices. Under
current law, there is no training that specifically addresses the needs
of LGBTQ+ patients. The training that this bill requires would help
bridge this gap between home health aides, personal care aides, personal
care staff, and certified nurse's aides who want to provide adequate
care and LGBTQ+ patients of all ages.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: S6223/A7589 Dinowitz

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

To be determined.

This act shall take effect immediately.
